authTierRationale: The only credential mode is an API Key: a Braintree public key + private key pair plus the merchant ID, all self-serve from the Braintree control panel. The CDK's TokenSource is constructed with oauth_spec=None and a BasicAuth credentials object, which base64-encodes username:password into an `Authorization: Basic ...` header. No OAuth app registration and no refresh token are involved.

unionMisfits.description: Every searchable stream needs TWO HTTP calls per bounded slice, and the schema's PullSpec holds only one path. Call 1 is POST {path}/advanced_search_ids with a JSON body {search: {<field>: {min, max}}} which returns only a list of IDs. Call 2 is POST {path}/advanced_search with a JSON body {search: {ids: [...]}} for chunks of at most 50 IDs, which returns the full records. I put the ids endpoint in `path` because it is what bounds the slice; the detail endpoint is unrepresented.

There is no server-side paginator on the search endpoints at all. Bounding is done by a client-driven date-window bisection: the connector calls advanced_search_ids for [start, end), and while the returned ID count is >= the search cap it halves the window (bisect_window) and retries; the resulting IDs are then chunked client-side into 50-ID detail requests fanned out concurrently. Caps are 10,000 IDs for non-transaction searches and 50,000 for transactions. `{"type":"none"}` is technically correct per-request but hides the real resumption mechanism entirely.

proposedShape.onCap: halve the window end and re-issue; raise if the window shrinks below 1 second

unionMisfits.description: The transactions incremental leg is a fan-out over NINE different search fields (authorization_expired_at, authorized_at, created_at, failed_at, gateway_rejected_at, processor_declined_at, settled_at, submitted_for_settlement_at, voided_at), unioned into one ID set, PLUS two extra lookback searches over the previous three days keyed on disbursement_date and dispute_date (each with its own nested created_at sub-windowing) because disbursement/dispute updates do not touch any of the nine fields. One PullSpec with one `path` and one `incrementalParam` cannot express this.

This connector is a hybrid, and neither `http` nor a vendor-SDK marker covers it cleanly. All HTTP is issued by the Estuary CDK's own HTTPSession (so real paths exist and are recorded above) — but the vendor `braintree` Python SDK (pinned ==4.34.0) is still imported and used for two things: choosing Environment.Sandbox vs Environment.Production, and constructing record objects (braintree.Transaction(gateway, dict), braintree.Dispute(dict), etc.) which are then flattened back into dicts. The wire format is also asymmetric: the request body is sent as JSON while the response is XML (Accept: application/xml) and is hand-parsed by a reimplementation of the SDK's XML coercion rules.

proposedShape.vendorSdkRole: record model construction and environment selection only, not transport

unionMisfits.description: Only the three INCREMENTAL_RESOURCES (credit_card_verifications, customers, subscriptions) ship a default re-backfill cron of `0 20 * * 5`. transactions and disputes are built by separate functions that omit `schedule` entirely, and the four full-refresh streams omit it too. Whether that asymmetry is deliberate is not stated anywhere in the source.

The disputes incremental cursor is a search over `effective_date` inside status_history, which the code's own comment says can be days apart from the record's updated_at — so the checkpoint watermark and the document's updated_at are not the same clock. Deduplication is handled out-of-band by the CDK's emitted_changes_cache (cache.should_yield). `cursorField` as a single string cannot say 'searched by X, watermarked by X, but the document's mutation time is Y'.

proposedShape.skewWarning: effective_date and updated_at can be days apart; dedupe via emitted_changes_cache
proposedShape.alternativeSearchField: received_date (DisputeSearchField enum, defined but unused by the current fetch paths)

abstained.streams[0].pull.snapshot.paginator.pageS: The merchant_accounts page size is never set by the connector; it reads `page_size` back off each response envelope and stops when the returned count is smaller. The server-side default is not stated anywhere in the source, so no literal value is recorded.
abstained.streams[0].pull.snapshot.paginator.limit: No limit/per-page parameter is sent — only `page`.
abstained.streams[8].pull.incremental.paginator.li: The disputes search sends only `page`; the 50-per-page figure comes from SEARCH_PAGE_SIZE being used to compute total_pages from total_items, not from a request parameter.
abstained.streams[7].cursorField: The transactions incremental leg has no single cursor field. It unions ID searches across nine timestamp fields and additionally re-searches disbursement_date and dispute_date over a three-day lookback; the checkpoint stored is the window-end datetime, not any one record field. Recording one name here would be misleading.
abstained.streams[*].pull.*.incrementalParam: Incremental bounding is not a query parameter. It is a nested JSON request body of the form {search: {<field>: {min, max}}} with ISO-8601 datetimes, so the `incrementalParam` shape (param + format) does not apply.
abstained.execution.defaultSchedule: There is no connector-wide schedule; every binding ships its own interval (PT5M) and, for three streams, a cron. Recorded per stream.
abstained.discovery: streamMode is static — the nine bindings are hard-coded lists in resources.py. No discovery mechanism exists.
abstained.transports[0].spec.baseUrl.value: The base URL is not constant: the host varies with advanced.is_sandbox and the path carries the merchant_id, so it is recorded as a template rather than a constant.
abstained.credentialModes[*].oauth: Braintree does support an OAuth flow in general, but this connector implements exactly one credentials variant (ApiKey, a BasicAuth subclass) and constructs TokenSource with oauth_spec=None. No OAuth mode is recorded because none exists in this code.
